description_full: Kongsberg Maritime ASA, along with its subsidiaries, provides products and systems for positioning and navigation, marine automation, onshore and offshore installations, merchant marine, and safety management solutions. Its products include bridge systems and control centres, deck machinery and cranes, electrical power systems, automation, digital solutions, naval, positioning, stabilisation and manoeuvring, propulsors and propulsion, tank monitoring, loading and stability, and simulation. The company also provides navigation and positioning systems, propulsion control systems, and automation and bridge systems, as well as hardware, and software and services. In addition, it provides cargo, fisheries and aquaculture, naval and coast guard, offshore oil and gas, offshore wind, passenger vessels, research, and workboats solutions. Further, it specializes in ship design; hydrodynamic research centre; engineering services; online services; and product disposal and recycling. It serves defense, maritime, oil and gas, and aerospace industries in Norway and internationally. The company was incorporated in 2025 and is headquartered in Kongsberg, Norway.

financial_summary: KONGSBERG MARITIME ASA is a mid-cap industrials business with a $5.5B market cap on $2.8B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +15% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder.
Returns on capital run at 36% against a 9% cost of capital — a 27-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat. Gross margins of 62% confirm genuine pricing power.

The business throws off $450M in free cash flow — roughly 16 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.26× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 0.8× net debt/EBITDA, and interest coverage of 12× is fortress-like.
Shareholder yield is only 0.0%, a thin return of capital, and insiders hold 53% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is.
